headline.label: BIGGEST RULES REWRITE
headline.subtitle: of the technical regulations changed vs 2022-2025
headline.source: FIA / Formula 1 — 'the most comprehensive rules overhaul in four decades'

2026.summary: 2026 is the first full regulation reset since 2022. The FIA has rewritten the technical regulations around active aerodynamics, a 50/50 hybridised power unit, sustainable fuels, and ground-effect floors. Roughly 70% of the technical regulations are new or substantively revised.

changes.title: Active aerodynamics: X-Mode and Z-Mode
changes.summary: DRS is replaced by two driver-selectable aero modes. X-Mode = high downforce (corners). Z-Mode = low drag (straights, ~+15-20 km/h).
impact: Removes the 'follow-the-leader' DRS problem
Straight-line speed gains come from low-drag configuration, not wing opening
Drivers manage mode selection on a corner-by-corner basis

changes.title: Front wing: narrower, simpler cascade
changes.summary: Front wing chord reduced from 2000mm (2022) to 1900mm. Cascade elements simplified. Outwash replaced by inwash to feed the underbody.
impact: Reduces outwash-induced wake that hurt following cars
Front-end aero balance shifts toward the floor
Cleaner airflow to the floor edge wing

changes.title: Floor edge wing + ground effect stronger
changes.summary: Floor edges now feature explicit edge wings. Venturi tunnels are deeper. The car is fully ground-effect-dependent.
impact: Floor is the primary downforce source
Ride height tolerance reduced (porpoising mitigation)
Cars run lower and stiffer than 2022-2025

changes.title: Sidepods: tapered look banned
changes.summary: The 2022-2025 'tapered' or 'coke-bottle' sidepod shape is no longer legal. Sidepod cross-section is now more strictly defined, with mandated cooling apertures.
impact: Reduces aerodynamic cleverness; pushes design to the floor and suspension
Cooling is now regulated by FIA-defined apertures, not free design
McLaren's 2024 advantage from sidepod design is wiped out

changes.title: Rear wing: lower-drag Z-Mode profile
changes.summary: Rear wing is significantly lower aspect in Z-Mode (straight-line config) than 2022-2025 DRS-open position. X-Mode (downforce) is the higher-drag cornering config.
impact: Top speed gains of ~15-20 km/h from Z-Mode
Trade-off: cornering downforce in Z-Mode is much lower than 2024 DRS-closed

changes.title: 50/50 ICE-electric split
changes.summary: MGU-K output tripled (120 kW → 350 kW cap, ~470 HP). ICE output capped at ~550 HP. Total system power ~1000 HP equivalent, with electric now nearly matching ICE.
impact: Lap-time delta: -3 to -4 seconds vs 2024
Energy deployment strategy becomes a real race factor
Manufacturers: Audi, Cadillac (GM), Red Bull-Ford Powertrains join; Honda stays; Renault/Alpine rebrand

changes.title: 100% sustainable fuel mandatory
changes.summary: All cars run on advanced sustainable fuel — drop-in fuel made from non-food bio feedstock, municipal waste, or captured CO2. The fuel must deliver equivalent performance to fossil gasoline.
impact: Net-zero carbon target in scope
Fuel development now a key manufacturer battleground
Aramco (Saudi), Shell, TotalEnergies, Mobil 1 supplying bespoke blends

changes.title: MGU-H removed
changes.summary: The heat-energy-recovery MGU-H (turbocharger-integrated) is deleted. MGU-K (kinetic recovery) is the only electric element. This removes the turbo-electrical complexity that defined 2014-2025 hybrid PUs.
impact: Simpler PU architecture — easier for new manufacturers to enter
Turbo lag returns as a design challenge
Lower cost of entry for Audi, Cadillac, Red Bull-Ford

changes.title: Power unit cost cap reduced
changes.summary: PU cost cap lowered to $95M/year (was $130M in 2022-2025). Includes spec parts (ECU, MGU-K, battery, control electronics) plus the manufacturer's ICE and turbo.
impact: Encourages new entrants by reducing spend
Forces manufacturer efficiency in design and supply chain
Customer engine deals (e.g. Red Bull-Ford) become attractive

changes.title: 30 kg lighter minimum weight
changes.summary: Minimum car weight drops from 798 kg (2024) to 768 kg. Drivers still weighed separately. Car is meaningfully lighter despite the larger battery and electric systems.
impact: Improved power-to-weight ratio (with PU bump)
Lower fuel-burn pace is now feasible
Drivers more sensitive to ballast placement for balance

changes.title: Stricter anti-porpoise measures
changes.summary: Vertical oscillation sensors mandated, AOM (Aero Oscillation Metric) limit enforced. Floor edge height min/max controlled more strictly than 2022-2023.
impact: Eliminates the 2022 porpoising drama
Forces teams to commit to a ride-height window
Floor flex tolerance reduced

changes.title: Halo + integrated headrest fairing
changes.summary: Halo structure unchanged at 9.5 kg titanium minimum. New for 2026: an integrated headrest fairing that's part of the survival cell.
impact: Aero: headrest fairing is part of the rear-wing airflow path
Safety: continues the post-2018 driver-protection standard

changes.title: Sprint weekend format revised
changes.summary: Sprint weekends now feature 1 sprint race (Saturday) + 1 feature race (Sunday). Practice and qualifying structure adapted. Sprint races do not award full championship points.
impact: Fewer sprint weekends overall (6 vs 2024's 8)
Sprint points reduced to 8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1 (top 8)
Sprint qualifying uses a separate session

changes.title: Engine allocation reduced
changes.summary: PU element allocations per season reduced (ICE: 4 → 3, MGU-K: 4 → 3, MGU-H removed). Exceeding allocation = grid penalties.
impact: Manufacturers must build durable PUs
Race-ending engine failures now heavily punished
Strategy: when to take a penalty becomes a key question

2025.summary: 2025 was the final year of the 2022-2025 regulation set. Minor aero and safety updates, no major technical reset.

changes.title: Floor edge height clarified
changes.summary: Floor edge height measurement clarified to close the 2024 flexi-floor loophole. Vertical flex tolerance reduced by 5%.
impact: Targets the McLaren / Mercedes-style flexi-floors of 2024
Affect on relative pace: minor
